subject: Discovery Recap — Pilot success criteria, approval path & commitment timeline
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Hammond <lisa.hammond@atlashealth.com>, Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery Recap — Pilot success criteria, approval path & commitment timeline

Hi Lisa / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned and we can turn this into a concrete pilot runbook. I’ve attached a short MPA draft and a proposed scope spreadsheet.

Key pain points you called out
- Entity linking failures in downstream workflows (esp. claims normalization) causing ~18% manual review load
- Current latency for batch inference (on your infra) prevents same-shift adjudication for higher-priority cases
- Data governance: requirement to keep PHI within your VPC and have audit logs for token-level retention

Pilot success criteria (agreed during call)
1) Accuracy: Reduce manual review volume by >=12 percentage points on the annotated sample set (Lisa to confirm acceptance threshold)
2) Latency: 95th percentile per-request latency < 800ms for inference path under target batch size
3) Security: SOC2 / infrastructure evidence on record; private deployment variant acceptable

Mutual Action Plan (high level)
- Nov 20 — Pilot scope sign-off (owner: Lisa Hammond) — deliverable: signed scope spreadsheet (attachment: pilot-scope.xlsx)
- Dec 8 — Procurement / PO issued (owner: Maria Lopez, Atlas Procurement)
- Jan 5, 2027 — Pilot start (duration 6 weeks) — target metrics measurement and weekly checkpoints
- Feb 16, 2027 — Pilot close & go/no-go decision (owners: Lisa, Tom + Redwood commercial lead)

Stakeholders / decision path
- Business sponsor: Lisa Hammond (VP Product) — final signoff for success criteria
- Technical sponsor: Tom Ruiz (Head of AI) — pilot acceptance for accuracy/latency
- Procurement: Maria Lopez — contract and PO
- Redwood: Rafael (you know me), Commercial: Lauren Bishop, Solutions: Aditya Rao

Open asks / risks
- Please confirm the acceptance threshold (exact percentage) for the accuracy criterion so the eval harness can be configured accordingly.
- We will need a quick SOC2 / security excerpt for your procurement team (I attached our SOC2 summary; if you prefer a private link we can send to Maria).
- If you prefer Dedicated capacity for predictable latency, we should lock a pricing band during procurement (Lauren / Aditya I’ve cc’d you to coordinate).

Next steps (for this week)
1) Lisa: review and sign the scope spreadsheet by Nov 20 (I’ve put redlines in the spreadsheet).
2) Rafael: prepare a short statement of technical approach for the pilot and a pricing options sheet by Nov 12.
3) Lauren / Aditya: prepare Dedicated vs Hosted cost comparators and a draft procurement note we can share with Maria.

Attachments: atlas-mpa-draft.pdf (MPA summary), pilot-scope.xlsx (scope + redlines)

If that matches your notes, I’ll update HubSpot and schedule the kickoff tentatively for Jan 5.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Lisa Hammond <lisa.hammond@atlashealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@atlashealth.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@atlashealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap — Pilot success criteria, approval path & commitment timeline

Thanks Rafael — this looks right and captures the discussion well. A couple of clarifications: 

- Accuracy threshold: we need at least a 15 percentage point reduction in manual review for the pilot to be considered successful. I’ll confirm formally with the analytics team but that’s the target.
- Procurement: looping in Maria (copied) so you can engage on PO timing and contract language. Maria — is Dec 8 workable for you to have a PO ready?
- SOC2: please send the SOC2 summary you referenced; procurement will need the report or a pointer to a secure link. If you can provide an excerpt of audit logging for data residency we can expedite.

Happy to sign the scope spreadsheet once we get the short technical appendix and SOC2 excerpt.

On timing: Jan 5 pilot start works for us provided procurement completes on schedule.

Thanks —
Lisa Hammond
VP Product, Atlas Health
Lisa.Hammond@atlashealth.com | +1 (617) 555-2244

Aditya — we need a short technical appendix (1 page) describing the deployment approach: private deployment option, audit logs for token retention, and how we’ll validate latency under the pilot load. If you can also add the minimal infra requirements we’ll include that in the scope doc.

Action items I’ll do: update the MPA with Lisa’s 15pp target, place the HubSpot record update (link below), and push the SOC2 summary to Maria via secure link.
